propositions: The snapshot janitor runs only in the review-bot process; all other hosts that resolve attested gates populate the snapshot store but never reclaim it, leading to unbounded storage growth.

The GC trigger must be operation-linked and execute as a near-free O(1) in-process check on the gate-resolution path, with heavy GC work delegated to a detached child process to avoid blocking the ticket store lock.

The trigger implementation uses stamp and worker-lock sidecars keyed on the per-host snapshot store root to coordinate single-flight GC passes across simultaneous worktrees, and respects or reclaims stale locks.

A non-review-bot host running attested gates will spawn a detached GC pass when the last-pass stamp is stale or missing, applying the existing janitor.run_gc policy without blocking the calling gate operation.

The design mirrors the compaction trigger pattern from compact_trigger.py, using a stamped file fast-path check, detached child execution with durable cwd, and shared flock coordination with the review-bot's resident janitor.
